title: Partitioned Daily Sales Write
description:
Finance closes the lake one business date at a time. The overnight sales drop usually mixes several calendar days into a single file, and re-runs for the same close date have been double-counting when they append instead of replacing that day’s slice.

Publish a clean daily sales fact for BUSINESS_DATE only — nothing from other days — laid out so consumers can read that date’s partition without scanning the whole lake, and so a re-run for the same date replaces prior output for that day.

Publish Parquet with overwrite. Output columns: txn_id, store_id, product_id, quantity, unit_price, business_date. Run uses smoke testcases; Submit row-diffs against each case’s expected/.

problemStatement.overview: Publish an idempotent, date-partitioned sales fact for BUSINESS_DATE.
symptoms: Multi-day drops land in one path and break daily consumers.
Re-running the same business date must not double-count.
yourTaskSteps: Keep rows where to_date(event_ts) equals BUSINESS_DATE; add business_date.
Write txn_id, store_id, product_id, quantity, unit_price, business_date with partitionBy("business_date").mode("overwrite").
Submit is graded with a row-level compare against each selected testcase expected/.
problemStatement.yourTask: Implement src/main.py that writes the daily partitioned sales drop for BUSINESS_DATE.
hints: BUSINESS_DATE is injected as an env string (YYYY-MM-DD).
Overwrite + partitionBy makes re-runs for that date idempotent for consumers reading the partition path.

gradeChecks: Spark job succeeds on selected Submit testcases
Only BUSINESS_DATE rows present; partitionBy business_date used
Each Submit testcase expected/ matches candidate rows
